messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on freeways, 35 mph on expressways, 25 mph on city streets.
• “No speed limit” zones exist in some rural areas. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle can result in a $50 fine. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations carry a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Failure to stop can lead to a $200 fine. | | **Parking** | • Parking on sidewalks, crosswalks, or in front of fire hydrants is prohibited.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing of vehicles is regulated; towing companies must be licensed.
• Unlawful towing can result in civil liability. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection. | | **Points System** | • Traffic violations accrue points on the driver’s record.
• Accumulating 12 points within 36 months can lead to license suspension. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage is required: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, and $25,000 for property damage. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 1–5) – covers all traffic regulations. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) website – provides forms, fees, and detailed explanations. - Texas Highway Patrol – publishes enforcement guidelines and updates. **Common Enforcement Practices** - Police may issue tickets for speeding, seat‑belt violations, cell‑phone use, and DUI. - Courts handle most traffic tickets; some may be resolved via online payment or traffic school. - Repeat offenders may face harsher penalties, including license suspension and mandatory education courses. **Resources for Further Information** - TxDMV: https://www.txdmv.gov/ - Texas Highway Patrol: https://www.txdps.state.tx.us/ - Texas Transportation Code: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.7.htm Feel free to let me know if you need details on a specific law or how to contest a ticket!
